title: Marginal QuestionPackage v1
description: Generated from tools/contract/fields.js. Structural validity only: capability is measured by the validator and reported by name, never enforced here, because a package that honestly sits at a lower capability is valid.

schema.description: says what kind of file this is, so a validator never guesses at content it cannot interpret.

version.description: the contract version this package was authored against.

type.description: whether the question shipped with the application or arrived through an import. Where a question came from is metadata beside its id and never part of it.

packageId.description: the authoring bundle this question arrived in, for tracing a set back to its source.

author.description: who authored the question, for review rather than for display.

authoredAt.description: when it was authored. A date, not a timestamp: nothing needs the minute.

reviewState.description: how far through review this question is. A draft may be imported and is never served to a student.

publication.description: whether a student may be given this question at all, independent of how complete it is.

notes.description: anything the next reviewer needs to know. Never rendered.

additionalProperties.description: every shared id this package references, by library. Generated from the package rather than authored beside it: a dependency list that can disagree with the package it describes is a second source of truth. The importer recomputes it and reports any difference in both directions, so an omitted library is caught as a mismatch rather than as a missing field.

shared records this package contributes to a library. A package may bring a record the library does not have. It may never replace one it does: a definition three other questions point at is not this import's to rewrite.

provides.description: May be null. Absent is a capability fact, reported by name, not a silent gap.

id.description: the stable name of this question in one namespace shared by bundled and imported questions alike. A collision is an import-blocking error and never an implicit overwrite.

subject.description: which subject's marking criteria, paragraph models and libraries apply.

topicRef.description: the syllabus node this question sits in. A ref, because the engine used to recover the topic from a display label with a keyword table: four word lists, first match wins, null if none hit. Names a record in the syllabus library.

topicLabel.description: the topic in words, for a subject that has no syllabus library at all. Never present beside topicRef: a question carries a ref or a label.

directive.description: the command verb, which decides the directive family and therefore every slot label, sentence shape and piece of guidance downstream. Nothing else decides it.

text.description: the question exactly as a student reads it. Every decode highlight anchors into this string.

marks.description: what the question is worth, which sets the expected length and the band table.

first.description: the first of the two ends this question joins. The sentence shapes bind to it by name. It is NOT vocabulary: it carries no meaning and is never displayed as a definition.

second.description: the second end. Both are present or neither is.

overallArgument.description: the one line the whole essay is arguing, which every paragraph is held against.

vocabRefs.description: the terms this question asks for by name. Vocabulary reaches a student because something named it, never because a term string appeared in prose.

studyRefs.description: the reading for this question. A resource is a label and a link to material the school already holds; no resource bytes live in this repository. Each names a record in the resources library.

intro.description: what this question's two ends actually are, in the author's words. It replaced a sentence the engine synthesised, which was only ever true of Operations questions.

id.description: the stable name of one claim the essay makes, so a pathway can point at it.

line.description: the claim as a student reads it in the planner.

label.description: the cause end of the claim, authored. The engine used to recover it by splitting the line on the word "to".

conceptRef.description: the concept record behind the cause end, so a student can open it. Names a record in the concepts library.

relation.description: how the left end acts on the right end. Authored, because the difference between shaping and constraining is the argument.

label.description: the effect end of the claim.

criterionRef.description: the objective or criterion the effect end names, so two questions arguing towards the same objective can be told they do. Names a record in the criteria library.

pathwayRefs.description: which authored arguments serve this claim, so the planner and the argument picker agree.

verbMeaning.description: what this directive verb demands, in this question, in plain words.

plainEnglish.description: the question restated so a student who stalls on its wording can still start.

anchor.description: the exact substring of question.text this note attaches to. It must appear in the text or nothing on screen can be highlighted.

note.description: what that part of the stem is asking for.

forEach.description: what has to be done for every element the question names.

decode.description: May be null. Absent is a capability fact, reported by name, not a silent gap.

concepts.description: the ideas a full answer has to use. Labels, not refs: this is the requirement rail, and it states what the answer must contain rather than opening a lesson.

relationships.description: the connections a full answer has to make, as distinct from the ideas it has to mention.

accomplish.description: what the answer as a whole has to achieve, which is what separates a complete response from a correct one.

syllabusSummary.description: the syllabus wording this question sits under, in the author's summary. Original words: syllabus text is not reproduced.

requirements.description: May be null. Absent is a capability fact, reported by name, not a silent gap.

mode.description: the shape the model answer takes. It does NOT decide the directive family: the command does, and a mode that disagrees with the command is the second answer to a settled question.

statement.description: the answer in one sentence, which the app compares a draft against.

acceptableThesis.description: what any acceptable thesis must contain, so a student's own wording can be accepted rather than matched.

checklist.description: what the finished answer must contain, item by item.

lean.description: which way a position leans. A judgement question that offers no qualified position is offering a choice between two absolutes.

id.description: the stable name of one criterion the judgement is made against.

coreAnswer.description: May be null. Absent is a capability fact, reported by name, not a silent gap.

base.description: the sentence the working answer builds from as the student picks arguments.

workingAnswer.description: May be null. Absent is a capability fact, reported by name, not a silent gap.

label.description: what the cause end of this question is called, so the app can tell a student their argument is running backwards.

forward.description: the direction the argument must run, stated once.

reasoning.description: May be null. Absent is a capability fact, reported by name, not a silent gap.

id.description: the question-local name of one element this question names. Question-local by decision: an area is whatever the question genuinely needs.

label.description: the element in the words a student reads. It is never matched against syllabus prose: matching a label against text is the inference this contract exists to remove.

syllabusRefs.description: the syllabus nodes this area claims to cover, if the author claims any. Claimed means resolved: a ref that names nothing is an error, and claiming nothing is valid. Each names a record in the syllabus library.

direct.description: the one line always shown for this slot when the student is writing about this area.

vocabRefs.description: terms this area asks for by name.

id.description: the stable name of one argument. It is written into saved sentences, so it can never change.

areaRef.description: which element of the question this argument belongs to.

short.description: the argument in four or five words, as it appears on the choosing card.

relationship.description: the relationship this argument asserts, in one line.

label.description: the cause end of this argument, authored. The engine carries an explicit rule that it is never derived from `short` or `relationship`, which is what makes it semantic rather than presentational.

conceptRef.description: the concept record behind the cause end. Names a record in the concepts library.

choiceMeaning.description: what choosing this argument commits the student to. Without it the picker is a list of labels and a student cannot tell what they are choosing between.

whatToProve.description: what this paragraph has to establish for the argument to hold.

commonMistake.description: the mistake students actually make on this argument, named before they make it.

status.description: whether the middle step of the relationship has been authored, is not needed, or has not been looked at.

text.description: the middle step: how the cause reaches the effect. It is the difference between an argument and an assertion.

conceptRef.description: the concept this argument sits on, which is what the Learn button opens. Names a record in the concepts library.

syllabusRef.description: the syllabus node this argument is written against. Replaces a {topic, section, point} prose triple matched by PREFIX: nine of the twenty-eight authored triples resolve only that way, so "rewards" finds "rewards - monetary and non-monetary, individual or group, performance pay". Names a record in the syllabus library.

learningRef.description: the lesson that teaches this argument to a student who does not know the content. A pathway may REFERENCE teaching; it may not contain a lesson. Names a record in the lessons library.

status.description: whether this argument has been through learning review. `none-required` is an authored decision that the argument needs no lesson, and is not the same as nobody having looked.

ref.description: the evidence record this argument uses. Replaces a display LABEL matched case-insensitively against the bank, where two records sharing a label silently became one. Names a record in the evidence library.

role.description: what this item is doing for THIS argument. Authored, never inferred: a record in the same topic is topic-context and nothing stronger, and even that is a claim the author makes.

why.description: why this item supports this argument. It belongs to the pathway; the record belongs to the library.

limits.description: what this item does not prove, so a student does not claim more than it supports.

direct.description: the one line always shown for this slot. `guides` and `help` were two fields for one idea; this is that idea with two depths.

rung.description: which step of the escalating ladder this is. Order is the meaning: each rung gives more than the one before it, and a full ladder is five rungs.

vocabRefs.description: terms this argument asks for by name.

role.description: whether this argument supports the judgement, limits it, or holds conditionally. A judgement question offering only support is offering a case, not a judgement, so pathway-guided requires at least one limitation.

source.description: whether the marking guidance was authored for this question or assembled from the subject's criteria.

bands.description: band descriptors. Present only with a source: marking language is quoted from somewhere or it is invented, and inventing it is the one thing this app may never do.

bandSource.description: where the band descriptors came from.

VocabRef.description: A term asked for by name. A bare term string here is the pattern the format replaced.

VocabularyRecord.title: VocabularyRecord
VocabularyRecord.description: Lives in the vocabulary library. Resolvable from: question, area, pathway.

subject.description: what it means in this course, which is usually narrower than the plain sense. A record with a term and no subject meaning is a word with nothing attached, which is the thing this library exists to prevent.

plain.description: what the word means in ordinary English, for a student who has never met it. Without it the record still teaches on the Learn surface and is not offered in the vocabulary panel.

example.description: the term doing its job in a sentence, in a context other than this question.

ConceptRecord.title: ConceptRecord
ConceptRecord.description: Lives in the concepts library. Resolvable from: pathway, learning.

requiresTeaching.description: whether this concept always needs teaching, needs it only in context, or never does. It was authored as the boolean true and as the string "contextual", and a field with two types is an unknown-enum fault waiting to happen.

vocabRefs.description: the terms this concept defines, as refs. Concepts used to own {term, meaning} pairs directly, which made two definition systems; vocabulary has one authority and this is how a concept points into it.

EvidenceRecord.title: EvidenceRecord
EvidenceRecord.description: Lives in the evidence library. Resolvable from: pathway.

source.description: where the fact came from. 0 of 58 records currently carry one, so no question can reach evidence-complete today. That is the report telling the truth about the content, and the requirement is not weakened to make the top state reachable.

verify.description: that the figure moves and the student should check a current one themselves.

SyllabusNode.title: SyllabusNode
SyllabusNode.description: Lives in the syllabus library. Resolvable from: question, area, pathway.

legacyTerms.description: the term strings that sit beside a syllabus point in the source content. They have no meanings anywhere. Topic matching and the learning allowlist read them; nothing displays them, and they can never satisfy a vocabRef, because a ref names an id and a term string in a ref position is an error.

ResourceRecord.title: ResourceRecord
ResourceRecord.description: Lives in the resources library. Resolvable from: question, area, pathway.

url.description: where the material is. A link to what the school already holds, behind whatever access that platform applies. No resource bytes live in this repository.
